items.title: id(world/replication): SignedReplicationEnvelope::sign refuses envelopes every receiver rejects (#6469)
items.body:
Closes #6469

## What

`SignedReplicationEnvelope::sign` now refuses every envelope that fails an envelope-local rule `ReplicationTracker::accept` enforces, instead of only refusing a wrong-source key and an over-bound payload:

- unsupported envelope version
- journal header version outside `JOURNAL_VERSION..=MAX_JOURNAL_VERSION`
- payload digest not equal to `payload_digest(payload)`
- payload not chaining to `cursor_after` (including malformed / undecodable payload)
- snapshot whose `cursor_before` is not the chain base for its world/source/header version
- terminal with a non-empty payload or `cursor_before != cursor_after`
- snapshot/tail payload whose journal header disagrees with the envelope (#4486 rule)

The checks live in a new `validate_envelope_local` helper that returns the same `ReplicationError` `accept` would name; `sign` maps any error to `None`. Receiver-state rules (world/pinned source, session nonce, `prev_frame_digest`, tail cursor position / snapshot version vs. the tracker's current chain) stay receiver-only, as the issue scopes them. The `sign()` doc comment now states the full refusal contract.

## Tests

- New `sign_refuses_envelopes_every_receiver_would_reject` pins all eight refused shapes from the issue at the signer, with a valid-constructor control that still signs `Some` and is accepted by a fresh tracker.
- Existing receiver tests that intentionally sign lying envelopes now build them through bypass helpers (`sign_bypass` in `replication::tests`, the existing `sign_unbounded` in `replication_receiver::tests`), per the acceptance criteria — never through the production `sign()`.
- `cargo test --manifest-path pkgs/id/Cargo.toml --lib replication`: 47 passed.
- Full `id` lib suite: 2505 passed + 332 passed, 0 failed (laptop, 2026-11-09).

Oracle: `ReplicationTracker::accept`'s envelope-local refusals — a frame the production signer produces must never be one every receiver rejects on envelope-local grounds.

items.title: test(id-worlds): pin sign refusal for a snapshot claim disagreeing with its payload header (#12218)
items.body: ## Problem #12039... correction: #12218 reported that a signed snapshot could claim a supported journal header version different from its payload's own `Created` header version and be committed with a self-inconsistent authenticated version. Queue triage (tasks 20905/20906) verified on current main (`081e841019`) that the reported defect **does not hold**: `validate_payload_journal_header` (`world/replication.rs:559-623`) enforces both `world_id` and `version` agreement at sign time (`validate_envelope_local` → `SignedReplicationEnvelope::sign`) and at accept time (`ReplicationTracker::accept`), and the accept-side shape is already pinned by `snapshot_and_tail_payloads_must_carry_the_journals_own_header` (ran live: 1 passed). ## Solution The triage pass left one gap: the #6469 sign-surface test (`sign_refuses_envelopes_every_receiver_would_reject`) covered the missing-header shape but not the supported-but-mismatched-claim shape. This branch (commit 42ce49f944, from that triage pass) adds exactly that case with a matched control to `sign_refuses_envelopes_every_receiver_would_reject` — the only file changed is `pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/world/replication.rs`, test-only, +26 lines. ## Verification - `cargo test --manifest-path pkgs/id/Cargo.toml -p id-worlds --lib sign_refuses_envelopes_every_receiver_would_reject` on the branch head `42ce49f944`: 1 passed (run through `~/tools/fleet-build-lock`). - Test-only diff; no production code changed. Per `.github/ci-policy.md` no automated PR check is a merge requirement; focused manual verification is the merge evidence. Closes #12218 (already-guarded per both triage verdicts on the issue; this PR pins the sign-time side so the scenario stays covered). --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: fix(id-worlds): refuse replication payloads carrying over-version entries at admission (#7970)
items.body: Closes #7970. ## Problem `ReplicationTracker::accept` chained Snapshot/Tail payloads without checking that each entry is admitted by the frame's journal header version — `chain_payload` proved only that every line decodes as a `JournalEntry`. Restore refuses any entry whose `journal_version_required_by` exceeds the journal header version, so a signed, in-range frame could carry an entry its header does not admit (e.g. a `PortalGrantSet`, requires version 10, under a version-1 header): the verified cursor advances over it, the durable receiver commits it, and the replica then refuses its own journal at the next restore — the same brick-at-next-open shape #4486 closed for journal headers. A real writer can never produce this frame (it bumps the header before appending such an entry); this is the writer-bug / forged-stream hole, closed at admission. ## Change - New `validate_payload_entry_versions` in `world/replication.rs`, mirroring the #4486 `validate_payload_journal_header`: for Snapshot/Tail payloads, decode each entry and refuse the first whose `journal_version_required_by` exceeds `envelope.header_version`. - New typed error `ReplicationError::EntryRequiresNewerJournal { required, header }` (the dedicated variant the issue left to the implementer). - Wired into both `accept` (Snapshot and Tail arms, alongside the header check, before any state changes) and `validate_envelope_local`, so the production signer also refuses to produce a frame every receiver would refuse (#6469). ## Tests - New regression test `snapshot_and_tail_payloads_must_not_carry_over_version_entries`, mirroring the #4486 set: over-version snapshot refused with cursor untouched; over-version tail refused after a valid snapshot; production signer returns `None` for the same envelope; control — the same entry under a version-10 snapshot is accepted end to end. - Replication module: 62 passed / 0 failed. Full `id-worlds` suite results in the PR thread / issue note. - `cargo fmt -p id-worlds --check` clean. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: id: F12.13 phase 5 slice 5 — authenticated replica sidecars (#806)

labels.name: audit:completed-later
labels.description: Gap completed by later merged PR

items.body: Slice 5 of F12.13 phase 5 for #806 (task 15853), remainder item 1: authenticated provision/refresh of the replica's active module artifacts and directory authorization facts. **Before:** the signed replication stream carried journal bytes only. A replica's `directory.jsonl` and `modules/` were local sidecars, planted out-of-band and fixed at open — unauthenticated, and never refreshed by replication. **Now:** - **Protocol (`world/replication.rs`)** — new `ReplicationKind::Directory` and `ReplicationKind::Module` frames. A sidecar frame carries no journal entries and must sit exactly at the chain cursor its batch has already reached (new `ReplicationError::SidecarCursorMismatch`), so the frame-digest chain binds the sidecars to the verified cursor they were captured at. Constructors `ReplicationEnvelope::directory / `::module`; signer-side local validation mirrors the tracker (#6469 pattern). - **Receiver (`world/replication_receiver.rs`)** — sidecar payloads stage beside the journal bytes and install only at the batch's terminal commit: directory facts atomically replace `directory.jsonl` (chunks pre-validated as complete `DirectoryEntry` lines before the tracker sees them), module bytes are stored content-addressed under `modules/` via `ModuleDir::save`. A truncated/refused/aborted batch leaves the previous committed sidecars untouched. Sidecars install before the journal, which remains the commit point; a crash in between leaves the old journal paired with sidecars the open path filters by the journal's own subjects and module hash. - **Feed (`world_replication_net.rs`, `world/actor.rs`, `world/handle.rs`)** — at every snapshot (initial sync and compaction/header resets) the writer serves the directory facts for the snapshot journal's subjects (one actor round trip, `WorldCommand::ReplicaSidecars` → `Directory::replica_facts_for`) and the active module's bytes, loaded from its content-addressed store under the actor's active hash (a load failure aborts the stream rather than serving a journal whose program the replica could never restore). The facts frame is always sent (an empty one replaces the replica's facts with none); the module only when the writer holds the bytes. - **Open path unchanged** — facts are selected per journal subject (`replica_facts_for` in restore) and a module loads only when its bytes hash to the journal-named hash, so provenance is the pinned source's signature and activation stays bound by the verified journal. **Tests** (oracle: the packet acceptance — modules hash-checked, facts authenticated to pinned source/cursor, refreshed with replication): - replication suite 57/57, including new: sidecar frames sit at the reached cursor and move nothing; an off-cursor sidecar is refused with state untouched; the signer refuses a sidecar with unequal cursors. - Receiver, new: sidecars commit with the snapshot and only at its terminal frame (chunked module reassembles content-addressed); an aborted later batch leaves the committed sidecars byte-identical; a malformed facts frame is refused before the tracker with nothing committed. - Full lib suites: id-worlds 797 passed / id-cli 671 passed, 0 failed. `cargo check -p id-worlds -p id-cli` clean; `cargo fmt` applied. (Clippy is currently unrunnable against the pooled target — E0514 rustc mismatch in the broker pool, pre-existing infra, not this change.) **Remainder after this slice** (recorded on #806; #806 stays open): resilience exercises on the durable path — writer outage, restart, reconnect, compaction/reset without journal loss or Records drift (reconnect on the follow path is implemented; lease-expiry is covered by PR #9407's tests). Refs #806. Task 15853 stays open for the resilience remainder. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: test(id): salvage probe_replication_sign characterization test from archive PR #7533

labels.name: audit:no-issue
labels.description: No spawning issue; judged on stated intent

items.body: ## Summary Salvage of the unique remainder of closed archive PR #7533 (batch #7297, routed by task 13841, worked as task 14211): re-applies `pkgs/id/tests/probe_replication_sign.rs` — the only file in #7533, absent from current main — verbatim onto current main. The file is a characterization probe for the replication signing path: `SignedReplicationEnvelope::sign` signs envelopes every receiver rejects. Its single test asserts a valid tail envelope signs and is accepted (control), and that eight dead-on-arrival shapes are refused by `ReplicationTracker::accept` with the specific `ReplicationError` variants: unsupported envelope version, journal header version 0 and above max, payload digest mismatch, cursor chain mismatch, malformed payload, terminal carrying a payload, snapshot before-cursor not at the chain base, and a snapshot journal header naming another world. ## Evidence - Closed PR #7533 verified this shift to contain exactly this one file; the file does not exist on current main (task 13841's content-level triage: 162 unique added lines, all in this file). - Local compile/test on the laptop could not complete within the shift's windows: the `id` crate build under current fleet load exceeded three 560s targeted-test attempts and one 560s `cargo check` attempt (dependency graph fully compiled and cached; the `id` lib compile itself is the long pole, and no compile *errors* were emitted before the timeouts — the runs died on time, not on diagnostics). CI is therefore the compile/test verdict for this salvage, per the fleet's CI-first doctrine. - If CI shows the world/replication API has drifted since the probe was written (2026-11-04), the salvage should be fixed forward in this PR or closed with that evidence — task 14211's packet explicitly allows a superseded outcome instead of forcing a landing. ## Merge Danger **Door:** two-way **Blast Radius:** minimal — one new integration test file under `pkgs/id/tests/`; no production code changes. Refs #7297 --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: feat(id): wire loc.position/loc.watch into the world actor (#2341 slice 2)
items.body: Implements #2341 slice 2 (slice 1's pure core landed in PR #5317, in pkgs/id/crates/id-caps): host wiring for `loc.position` / `loc.watch` in the world actor, mirroring how `time.now` / `time.tick` and the `device.info` host seam are wired. ## Change - **Core (id-caps):** `Subscription::LocWatch(u64)` — `loc.watch` and `loc.watch:` specs now parse through `parse_loc_watch_interval_ms` (bare spec takes the 5s floor; sub-floor/malformed specs stay `Unknown` for the actor to refuse), with cap `"loc.watch"` and a canonical spec form. - **Actor seams:** `WorldActor` gains the host location/consent seams beside `device_manifest`: `location_consent` (default `ConsentRequired`) and `location_fix` (default `None` — the default host has no location source), plus armed `loc_watches`. Production construction (world/handle.rs) starts from the same defaults, so a stock host refuses sensor uses rather than fabricating fixes. - **`loc.position` execution:** after the ledger's generic decision, the consent seam's refusal is returned verbatim (`consent_required` / `os_permission_denied`); no fix is `no_fix`; a fix less precise than the request's optional `max_accuracy_m` is refused via `refuse_beyond_ceiling` (`precision_ceiling`), never silently degraded; otherwise the reading's wire object is the result. - **`loc.watch` lifecycle:** malformed/sub-floor specs are refused once per spec (subscription_refused_event, as with sub-floor ticks); granted watches arm on presence only while consent stands, join `next_deadline`, and fire from the run loop beside ticks. A due watch delivers `loc_watch_reading_event` when a fix exists and nothing when none does. If consent has been withdrawn, the watch is closed with exactly `loc_watch_revocation_event()` and removed from the active subscriptions. ## Tests - New (all passing): `loc_position_refuses_until_the_consent_seam_grants` (both refusal codes), `loc_position_is_no_fix_when_the_host_source_has_none`, `loc_position_refuses_a_fix_beyond_the_precision_ceiling` (refusal + in-ceiling success), `loc_watch_delivers_readings_and_revokes_on_consent_withdrawal` (reading delivered on interval; withdrawal → exactly the revocation event, watch disarmed and closed). - Regression: `cargo test world::` in pkgs/id 308/308; id-caps crate 83/83. (Sensor caps sit outside the default ceiling by design, so the test worlds name them in the ceiling as well as granting them — the slice-1 test pattern.) 🤖 queue worker lane any-b, task 9301 --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added location-watch subscriptions that can provide periodic location readings when consent is granted and a location fix is available. * Location readings can be limited by a maximum accuracy requirement, and report how long ago the fix was received. * **Behavior Changes** * Location watches stop when consent is withdrawn, the subscription ends, or presence is no longer active. Consent withdrawal also triggers a revocation event. * Requests with invalid location-watch settings or more than the supported number of watches are rejected.
